Source: http://news.bbc.co.uk

Posted September 29, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: This story is important for three reasons.

First, it puts more political pressure on the Blair government to end their heartless stalling on medical marijuana.

See
Scottish Authorities Drop Prosecution Of Crippled Medical Marijuana Grower;
The Economist Reports On The UK’s Legal Medical Marijuana Grower

Second, it is yet another instance of jury nullification, which is apparently easier to do in the UK than in DEAland.
See
UK Medical Marijuana Grower Acquitted By Jury –
Life A " Living hell " With Conventional Pharmaceuticals
and
Acquittal Of UK Medical Marijuana Co-Operative Operator Gets Massive Media Coverage
– There, Not Here, Of Course –
" Cannabis Law In Chaos As Dealer Is Cleared " -- 5 Articles
and
For more on jury nullification see theFully Informed Jury Associationwebsite

Third, it is based on medical necessity, not just a philosophical disagreement with marijuana prohibition. Recall that the federal government would not let Todd McCormick and the late Peter McWilliams even mention their medical histories, much less talk about medical marijuana -- even though they were relying on a state medical marijuana law.)
See
The Murder of Peter McWilliams -- An Indictment, Not an Obituary – by Richard Cowan

MS Sufferer Cleared Of Cannabis Charge

A woman with multiple sclerosis was yesterday cleared of a criminal charge of possessing cannabis, after telling a court that she needed it to relieve the symptoms of the muscle wasting disease.

The public gallery cheered as Lezley Gibson, 36, was found not guilty by a jury of seven women and five men after only an hour and a half. She had denied one charge of possessing eight grams of the class B drug, worth UKP40, on the grounds that she needed it for medical reasons.

Outside court, flanked by her husband, Mark, Mrs Gibson said she would continue smoking cannabis and called for a change in the law:

" There are hundreds of people like me out there. No one in my position should have to be dragged through the courts like this, but I am glad it is all over. I feel brilliant. " She intended to throw a party to celebrate.
(MarijuanaNews note: Unfortunately, there are many more MS patients in the UK who still have to risk arrest to use marijuana. The UK MS Society, unlike its DEAland counterpart has been supportive of patients who use marijuana. They estimate that over 1,000 are already doing so illegally.)
See
UK To Spend 3 Years And A Million And Half Dollars On Tests
To Find Out If Marijuana Helps MS Patients,
But Will Do No Research To See If Arresting Them Is Harmful.

During the four day trial the jury heard that police raided her home in Alston, Cumbria, in August of last year and found cannabis.

She told the court she began smoking 12 years ago, three years after being diagnosed with MS at 21. She had tried steroids, valium, hypnotherapy and acupuncture but none of them helped relieve the symptoms, which include spasms, dizziness and loss of feeling, but nothing made her feel as well as cannabis.
See
Meanwhile UK Painkillers Kill 2,000 Per Year. But They Are Sold Over-the-Counter So They Must Be Safe!

She smoked up to five joints a day bought from dealers, because it enabled her to have a more normal life: " I would use paint stripper if I thought it would make me well. "

The prosecution did not accept Mrs Gibson had the defence of necessity, because she did not need to smoke cannabis to avoid death or serious injury from her condition.
(MarijuanaNews note: The jury obviously rejected this very narrow view of necessity, as did the DEAland 9th Circuit in their ruling. Unfortunately, the Clinton Administration does not care.)
See
Federal Judge Allows Oakland CBC to Sell Medical Marijuana To Seriously Ill Who Have No Alternatives. Government Offers No New Arguments Against It. Appeal To Supreme Court Expected.
and
Supreme Court Grants Emergency Stay Against Oakland CBC. Arbitrary Power Trumps Basic Rights.
and links

Graham Knowles, prosecuting, told Mrs Gibson: " Your preference is to break the law with no need to do so by buying cannabis from drug dealers because you greatly value the relief that you sincerely believe you get from cannabis.

" It wasn't necessary at any time for you to use cannabis, " he said.
(MarijuanaNews note: Is that what would he have said, if he had been the one in pain?)
